meta.dataset: SBA loan add-on screen: PPP, 7(a) and 504 borrowers matched to the six BSP companies
meta.title: SBA loan screen
meta.method: We read every loan in the SBA Paycheck Protection Program release and every SBA 7(a) and 504 file from FY1991 to date, and kept the borrowers whose industry code and location match a BSP company: residential HVAC, plumbing and electrical near Lancaster PA and Toms River NJ for Punctual Pros; New England electrical and water and sewer contractors for CET; computer services firms for Frontline; lab, scientific and chemical supply wholesalers for Thomas Scientific; public relations and opinion research firms for BPI; apparel makers and clothing wholesalers for Fair Harbor. First and second PPP draws and name variants were merged into one business, and each business was linked to its 7(a) and 504 loans by name and ZIP code or name and city. BSP companies and their add-ons were removed. Companies already on a hand-built target list stay in and are marked. A ranked shortlist per company was built from the loan records: the jobs figure, distance to the hub, the industry words in the name and any recent SBA loan; a company known only from loans made before FY2010 is kept in the records but not shortlisted. Ownership was then classified by Claude agents acting as a typed decision model: each agent read public web evidence (the company's own website, state business records, press releases and news, and search-engine result snippets) and returned one of eight labels (founder-led, family next generation, employee or partner-owned, sponsor-backed or acquired, franchise unit, closed, out of segment, unknown) with a probability for each and the evidence behind it. Every founder-led or family call was then sent to a second agent for an independent re-check for a sale, a parent company or an investor; one record arrived in part, without its re-check, and is marked so. Where the second agent's own deal searches could not run, the call is marked as confirmed from the company site only and scores lower, and a later review overturned one call. Review counts and ratings come only from search-engine snippets and companies' own websites; no review site was scraped, and no reviewer names are kept. Jev, TypeSafe AI's decision API, was not used because no account was available; scripts/classify_ownership.py makes the same decision through either provider. PPP jobs are what borrowers reported in 2020 and 2021. The 7(a) and 504 data run from FY1991 to 2026-09-30, and each company shows its latest SBA loan, the jobs that loan supports, and whether the loan financed a change of ownership. The fit score adds six parts shown in fit_formula; tiers use the engine's thresholds, and Tier 1 needs a fully confirmed call. Each company then got a short profile from its own website where one was found: what it does (specialties), who it serves, where it works and any headcount it states. Staff is that stated headcount with its source page, or else the latest jobs figure on its SBA loans, labelled either way. No company states its revenue, so revenue is modelled (est.) in 2025 dollars from US Census Statistics of U.S. Businesses 2022 benchmarks and the company's SBA loan data: the stated US headcount or else the loan jobs figure times Census receipts per employee for its industry and size, and, for PPP borrowers, the PPP loan turned back into payroll and divided by the Census payroll share. The estimate is the midpoint of the two, with a low-high range and a confidence; see revenue_model.

fit_formula.segment_fit: 0-30. Checked companies: 30 x (1 - the probability it is out of segment). Unchecked: 18 when the name carries a segment signal, else 12.
fit_formula.size: 0-20. Latest jobs figure inside the ideal band: 20; elsewhere inside the screen band: 12; outside: 5.
fit_formula.ownership: 0-30. Label points: founder-led 30, family next generation 27, employee or partner-owned 18, unknown 10, franchise unit 4, sponsor-backed or acquired 0, closed or out of segment 0. A call the re-check fully confirmed (its own deal search ran) scores its label points; any other checked company scores the probability-weighted average of the label points; an unchecked company scores 10.
fit_formula.proximity: 0-10, Punctual Pros and CET only. Straight-line miles from the ZIP centroid to the nearest hub or site: 30 or less 10, 60 or less 7, 90 or less 4, farther 2.
fit_formula.verification: 0-5. Independent re-check confirmed 5; confirmed from the company site only, with no deal search, 3; re-check could not confirm, or the call was corrected on review, 1; not run or record received in part 0.
fit_formula.evidence: 0-5. Company's own site 2, press or news 2, state or SBA record 1, any other source 1.
fit_formula.scaling: Segments with no proximity part are scaled from 90 to 100 points.
fit_formula.cap: A company already sold to a sponsor or roll-up, or closed, is capped at 40. Tier 1 needs a fully confirmed call, an operating company and no sale, rebrand or shared applicant-tracking warning; any other company is capped at 79.
fit_formula.tiers: Tier 1 80 or more; Tier 2 65 to 79; Tier 3 50 to 64; Tier 4 below 50.

caveats: PPP jobs are what the borrower reported in 2020 or 2021, not a current headcount. Where a later 7(a) or 504 loan exists, its jobs figure is used instead; the lender reports it and SBA does not check it.
Reading 'Change of Ownership' in the SBA business-age field as a loan that financed a purchase is our interpretation; the SBA dictionary does not define it further.

Ownership comes from public web evidence only. A founder-led or family label means no sale, parent or investor was found, not that the owner has confirmed it. Most re-checks that backed a founder or family call could not run their own deal searches; those calls are marked as confirmed from the company site only, score lower and cannot reach Tier 1.

7(a) and 504 loans go back to FY1991. A company known only from loans made before FY2010, with no PPP loan, stays in the loan records but is not shortlisted, since nothing on record shows it still operates.
Review counts and ratings are as shown in search-engine snippets or on the company's own site; they were not checked on the review sites.
Ownership checks cover the shortlist for all six companies, with a second, skeptical pass on every founder or family call.
PPP is a weak source for Fair Harbor: apparel makers in the loan data are mostly contract sewers, uniform makers and small boutiques, so few branded swim or apparel companies appear.
Distances are straight lines from the ZIP centroid, not drive times.

Revenue for loan-screen companies is modelled from Census benchmarks and SBA loan data, not reported. Each figure carries a low-high range (the high end is a median 1.7 times the low end) and a confidence. The range covers the two methods and the spread between Census size classes; no model price is shown when its high end is more than 4 times the low end. Census figures are national averages for an industry and size, and a company can sit well above or below them. On the 15 companies that are also on a hand-built list, the model reads a median 1.7 times the vendor figures those lists use, mostly because the vendor assumes lower revenue per employee. So loan-screen and hand-built revenue are shown and summarised apart.

Staff for loan-screen companies is the headcount the company states on its website where it gives one (11 companies), else the jobs figure on its latest SBA loan, which may be several years old. The revenue model uses the stated headcount when it covers the US business only, else the loan figure.

full_data.note: Every SBA column and row that matches each segment, unfiltered, as published loan files; items carry full_data_keys to find their own rows.

revenue_model.what: Revenue (est.) for every loan-screen company, from scripts/estimate_revenue.py run on the item.
revenue_model.dollars: 2025 dollars (CPI-U); a stated figure is as stated

methods.headcount: Staff the company states for its US business, else the latest loan jobs figure, x Census receipts per employee for the industry and size class.
methods.payroll: PPP loan (first draw, else second draw) x 12 / 2.5 = payroll, less benefits (BLS), / the Census payroll share for the industry and size class, then CPI-U to 2025.
methods.stated: Revenue the company states; overrides the model. Companies with one: 0.

revenue_model.range: Lowest method x (1 - s) to highest x (1 + s); s is the gap to neighbouring Census size classes, 10% to 40%. It covers the two methods and the spread between Census size classes, not how far one company can sit from its class average.
revenue_model.confidence: High: the two methods agree within 25%. Medium: within 60%, or one method alone. Low: further apart, a thin Census cell, or a data warning. The portal shows a loan-screen estimate at medium confidence at most, since it is modelled.
revenue_model.checks: PPP payroll per reported job above $100K plus benefits: the payroll method sets only the range. Below $20K: the jobs figure or the loan is wrong, so a consistent second draw replaces the first, or else the headcount method sets only the range.

vs_hand_built.note: Model estimate / the hand-built list's vendor-modelled figure, same company.

build_inputs.note: candidates and zcta are working files kept outside the repo (scripts/build_ppp_screen.py output and the Census ZCTA gazetteer).
